quandoUsar: Strip of three or four highlight numbers on a landing or corporate page, each with a minimal chart that backs it up: trend, availability, distribution, or map.
When each number has a context line worth showing on demand, on hover or focus.
quandoEvitar: Use `metric-card` for a number with context in a dashboard; this strip is a page section and counts only once, when it enters the screen.
Use `animated-counter` when you only need a number that animates between values.
Use `bar-chart` or `line-chart` when the chart is the main content and the person needs to read values from it.

teclado.acao: Reaches each number that has `context`; with focus, the detail line gives way to the context line and the visual takes the accent color.

acessibilidade: Screen readers receive only the final value of each number, in hidden text; the animated count and the visuals are `aria-hidden`, so put in `detail` or `context` what the chart shows.
The strip is a `<section>` named by `title` (or “Key numbers”) and the numbers form a `<dl>`; `detail` and `context` both stay in the DOM, so both are read.
A number with `context` receives `tabIndex=0`, but the focus outline is removed: focus shows only through the line swap and the visual's color.
movimento: The first time 40% of the list enters the screen, the numbers rise in sequence (90 ms apart) and count from zero to the value in 1.6 s (`duration`); compact numbers count already in the final unit, from 0.0M to 2.3M.

When each number is almost at its value, the visual draws itself: line and map reveal from left to right, the bars grow in a wave and, in `divided`, the thin lines run across the strip and between the numbers.
With “reduce motion” on (read after hydration, with CSS covering the first paint), the numbers already appear at their final value and visuals and lines are ready, with no transition.
responsivo: The strip's container queries: up to 800 px the numbers go two by two and a strip of three stacks into one column; up to 520 px it goes one per row, with the visual beside the number.
The final width of each number is reserved from the start, so the count never pushes the layout.
desempenho: The count writes directly to the number's `textContent` on every frame, without re-rendering React, and `useInView` with `once` fires only once.
The `map` visual draws about 760 SVG circles, one per land point of the 80 × 30 grid, and is the heaviest of the four.
notasIA: Import the named component `StatsBand`; the default export is `StatsBandBlock`, the preview with layout switching, and `stats` uses the example data from `stats-band-data.ts`.

Each `Stat` takes `value`, `label` and, if you want, `prefix`, `suffix`, `decimals`, `notation: "compact"`, `detail`, `context`, and `visual` (`trend`, `uptime`, `distribution`, or `map`); the grid goes up to 4 columns.
`locale` is `en-US` by default so server and client format the same; use `pt-BR` for a decimal comma, and change the `key` to play the count again.
